THOUGHT: The patient has very high fever (104°F), autonomic instability (tachycardia, hypertension), marked muscle rigidity described as noncompliant to manipulation (suggesting "lead‑pipe" rigidity), altered mental status with somnolence/non‑responsiveness, markedly elevated CK and transaminases, and mild metabolic acidosis. This constellation strongly fits a hyperthermic syndrome with severe generalized rigidity and rhabdomyolysis. Serotonin syndrome usually presents with hyperreflexia and clonus and more agitation, which are not described. Sympathomimetic or anticholinergic toxidromes generally produce agitation, diaphoresis (sympathomimetic) or dry skin with mydriasis and less severe generalized rigidity (anticholinergic), and malignant hyperthermia requires anesthetic exposure. Although no antipsychotic exposure is documented in the history provided (a limitation), the clinical picture — lead‑pipe rigidity, hyperthermia, autonomic dysfunction, altered consciousness, and very high CK — is most consistent with neuroleptic malignant syndrome (or a NMS-like syndrome). Immediate management (not requested here) would include stopping offending dopamine‑blocking agents, aggressive cooling, IV fluids, monitoring/treating rhabdomyolysis, and consideration of dantrolene or bromocriptine as indicated.

DIAGNOSIS: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)
